Igor Andreevich D'iu, recruited via Telegram, has been charged in the US with acting as a Moscow agent in a surveillance campaign against employees of a defense technology company, understood to be Palantir. It shows how Russian services recruit proxies through messaging apps.


Physical and human targeting of defense tech staff is a counterintelligence signal for the sector.


Sources: The Record


AI & Machine Learning


Google releases Gemini 4 Neon (vendor announcement)


Nov 18, 22:34


Google announced Gemini 4 Neon on its blog. The post is the top AI story on Hacker News with 906 points and 711 comments. Capability and benchmark claims come from Google and are unverified.


A first-party frontier model release from Google that developers and enterprises will need to evaluate.


Sources: Google Blog · Hacker News


Nadella: AI is finding bugs at breakneck pace, making outages likelier; critical infrastructure 'unpatchable'


Nov 19, 00:58


At DealBook, Satya Nadella said AI tools are finding cybersecurity bugs very fast and that companies must deploy fixes 'instantaneously'. He downplayed the recent Outlook outage and said much critical infrastructure is unpatchable. Palmer Luckey blamed the recent tech outages on attackers using AI against outdated infrastructure. Five outlets covered the Nadella interview.


Two prominent leaders are framing AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery as a cause of the current outage wave.


Sources: NYT Business · TechCrunch · NYT Business (Luckey)


Senators urge White House to build national defensive AI cyber effort


Nov 18, 20:00


A bipartisan Senate pair called on the White House to launch a national effort to confront AI-enabled cyber threats more robustly. They cited recent security incidents involving AI.


It signals policy momentum toward funded, government-backed AI cyber defense.


Sources: The Record


NYC, LA and Chicago schools weigh dropping Google Search over forced Gemini bundling


Nov 19, 00:18


Google says that starting next year, schools can't disable Gemini-powered features without also losing Search. Google's education VP said 'Search and AI are deeply integrated'. NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Sen. Bernie Sanders criticized the move, and the three big districts are looking at alternatives. Two outlets reported it.


It's a test of how far vendors can bundle AI into core products against customer pushback.


Sources: The Verge · NYT Technology


Banks tell customers using AI agents they're on their own, even if hacked; Citi is the latest


Nov 18, 18:32


Citi has joined other major banks in putting the brakes on personal finance AI agents. The banks' position is that customers who use agents bear responsibility if those agents are compromised.


Liability for agent-driven transactions is being decided now, and banks are putting the risk on users.


Sources: TechCrunch


AI debt collection platform CreditNirvana exposed 6.6M accounts and 315,000 call recordings


Nov 18, 20:00


Two serious vulnerabilities in the CreditNirvana platform would have allowed attackers to access detailed sensitive data. That data included emails, texts and credit reports, as well as the call recordings.


An AI-powered back-office platform holding highly sensitive consumer data shows the security gap in fast-deployed AI services.


Sources: Wired


Technology


DHS Secretary says administration will push industry to share more on big patches before rollout


Nov 18, 21:00


At a House Homeland Security hearing, Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the administration will ask companies to share more information about big patches before they take effect. It follows a rough stretch of major tech disruptions.


The government is moving toward coordination on patch rollouts after the recent outage cascade.


Sources: The Record


Apple addresses outages hitting Apple Pay, iCloud and apps


Nov 19, 04:31


Apple acknowledged disruptions affecting Apple Pay, iCloud and apps. NYT says they followed days of unrelated problems that interrupted air travel and work at offices, schools and government. NYT also ran a guide on preparing for a prolonged digital disruption.


Another major platform outage adds to a week of cascading failures that has rattled users and regulators.


Sources: NYT Technology · NYT Technology (prep guide)


Waymo suspends driverless freeway rides nationwide after California pushback


Nov 18, 18:45


California told Waymo to leave freeways after incidents, including incursions into construction zones and a run-in with patrol vehicles. The operator has suspended driverless rides on high-speed roads nationwide.


A regulator-driven rollback of a leading autonomous service signals how fragile expansion is after safety incidents.


Sources: The Register


Judge approves Google's $10M purchase of defunct Spirit Airlines' data for AI projects


Nov 18, 21:39


A federal bankruptcy judge ruled Google can take Spirit Airlines' data for $10 million. Google agreed to protections and plans to use the data in AI projects.


Bankruptcy sales of customer data are becoming a source of AI training and project data.


Sources: The Record


GTA VI launch didn't break the internet thanks to multi-CDN and DNS routing


Nov 19, 06:57


The Register reports that multiple CDNs and routing users to nearby download sites kept traffic flowing for everyone. It's a rare infrastructure success story in a week of outages.


It's a practical example of resilience engineering for large traffic spikes.


Sources: The Register


MongoDB acquires Firebolt to merge transactions and analytics


Nov 18, 18:02


MongoDB bought Firebolt, aiming to bring transactional and analytical workloads under one roof. The Register notes many vendors have tried to combine the two. Deal terms were not in the report.


It shows database vendors consolidating around unified workloads as AI-driven demand grows.


Sources: The Register


Business & Markets


Anthropic prices record IPO at $83 a share, above range, valuing it above $1.5T (vendor announcement)


Nov 18, 23:11


Anthropic announced it priced its IPO of Class A shares at $83, above the projected range. NYT says it sold $81.3 billion of stock in a record offering at a valuation above $1.5 trillion. Shares begin trading Thursday on Nasdaq. Crunchbase notes $17B in revenue and over 11,900 customers spending $100K or more, along with large compute commitments. NYT adds it becomes the largest public benefit corporation.


This is the defining public-market event for AI and sets the valuation benchmark for every frontier lab.


Sources: Anthropic · TechCrunch · NYT Technology · Crunchbase News


Palo Alto Networks to buy AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5B in all-stock deal


Nov 19, 04:25


The deal gives Palo Alto a platform for fine-tuning and running open-weight AI models in public and sovereign clouds.


A multibillion-dollar security vendor move into AI model infrastructure points to continued consolidation.


Sources: SecurityWeek


Nvidia stock suffers worst run since 2008 as it delays its 10-Q and Kress reassures staff


Nov 19, 06:31


Nvidia is heading for a seventh straight weekly loss, per Euronews. TechCrunch reports it surprised the market by not filing its routine 10-Q for weeks. Interim CEO Colette Kress told employees at an all-hands to expect pay raises and more equity. Tech leaders including Sam Altman and Palmer Luckey voiced support for Jensen Huang, while Nadella said he stays confident in Nvidia.


Leadership turmoil at the key AI chip supplier is now showing up in its stock and its regulatory filings.


Sources: Euronews Business · TechCrunch · Wired · NYT Business


US tightens AI chip exports to China; Tencent says it 'sets everyone back'


Nov 19, 05:13


Washington announced plans to clamp down on China's access to AI chips, which Wired ties to the Nvidia spy scandal. Tencent's president said the ban sets everyone back in China but may spur its chip industry. NYT reports Alibaba used its AI computing to aid a lab linked to China's military. Wired says officials expect little AI progress from Trump's China trip.


Export controls are reshaping chip supply chains and AI market access just as the Trump-Xi talks begin.


Sources: The Register · NYT Business · Wired · Wired


Nadella: 60K Microsoft buyout offers were driven by AI, not another layoff


Nov 19, 01:42


At DealBook, Satya Nadella explained that in October he offered buyouts to 60,000 employees, urging voluntary exits rather than a massive layoff. He said the reason is AI, though not in the way you might expect. Two outlets covered it.


It shows how a major tech employer is restructuring its workforce around AI.


Sources: TechCrunch


Payhawk raises $280M at $2B valuation for AI-agent spend management


Nov 18, 20:29


Payhawk, founded in 2018, uses AI agents to help companies track and manage expenses and procurement. The raise values the enterprise financial management platform at $2 billion.


It's a large round showing investor appetite for agentic AI in finance operations.


Sources: TechCrunch
